Brief: Describe the Great Barrier Reef and the threats it faces. — about Tourism

1. Due to its vast biodiversity, warm clear waters and accessibility from the tourist boats called "live aboards", the reef is a very popular destination, especially for scuba divers.
2. Tourism on the Great Barrier Reef is concentrated in Cairns and also The Whitsundays due to their accessibility.
3. These areas make up 7–8% of the park's area.
4. The Whitsundays and Cairns have their own Plans of Management.
5. Many cities along the Queensland coast offer daily boat trips.
6. Several continental and coral cay islands are now resorts, including Green Island and Lady Elliot Island.
7. As of 1996, 27 islands on the Great Barrier Reef supported resorts.
8. In 1996, most of the tourism in the region was domestically generated and the most popular visiting times were during the Australian winter.
9. At this time, it was estimated that tourists to the Great Barrier Reef contributed A$776 million per annum.
10. As the largest commercial activity in the region, it was estimated in 2003 that tourism generated over A$4 billion annually, and the 2005 estimate increased to A$5.1 billion.
11. A Deloitte report published by the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority in March 2013 states that the Reef's 2,000 kilometres of coastline attracts tourism worth A$6.4 billion annually and employs more than 64,000 people.
12. Approximately two million people visit the Great Barrier Reef each year.
